newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU membership boosted Finnish security, ambassador says.
newsitem.headline: EU membership boosted Finnish security, ambassador says.

text.p: Finland's chief representative to the European Union painted a positive picture on Wednesday of the country's first two years in the EU, saying it had boosted security and lowered food prices.
"We are now in the world clearly a much more important partner, not just in Europe," ambassador Antti Satuli said in a speech at the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS).
He said superpowers such as the United States and Japan now listened to Finland, which joined the EU on January 1, 1995, with "a different kind of interest."
Membership had also increased the security and stability of Finland, which shares a long border with Russia. "It is a question of feeling, but that is how it is felt," he said.
Comparing Finland's situation with its western neighbour Sweden, which joined the EU at the same time, he said: "It is clear that Sweden has a more stable eastern neighbour than we."
In addition, Finland was now taking part in EU decision- making. "For the first time in history, Finns are sitting around the table where major European decisions are taken," Satuli said.
In contrast to the situation in Sweden, Finns are still about as much in favour of EU membership as they were at the time of the referendum in October 1994 when they voted to join the EU.
Satuli said this was partly explained by a realistic campaign ahead of the referendum. "What we promised would happen has taken place," he said.
In addition, both Finnish consumers and industry have seen the benefits of membership in the form of a 12 percent drop in food prices and increased investments.
Finland has also influenced EU policies, for example in the fields of transparency and environmental questions as well as in new initiatives for the Baltic and Barents seas.
Satuli said there was now a "northern dimension" of the EU.
"And I'm sure that in the future you will be hearing much more about this concept of northern dimension," he said.
Looking ahead, he said enlargement was a "necessity" and predicted that Finland would be in the first wave of countries in economic and monetary union (EMU).
